create.name: Joa Scetbon
create.bio:
Sensei Joa Scetbon is a French-American Zen teacher who grew up in and around Paris and has been settled in the city again since 1999. He came to meditation in the early 1990s with the American lama Surya Das, then found his main teacher in Catherine Genno Pagès Roshi at Dana Sangha in Montreuil, taking the precepts with her in 2000. From 2004 he trained with her first successor, Amy Hollowell Roshi, co-founded Wild Flower Zen Sangha with her and in 2021 became her first dharma heir, in the White Plum line of Taizan Maezumi Roshi. Outside the zendo he works as an editor and translator and has put books by Bernie Glassman and Stephen Batchelor into French.

His teaching is lay Zen for people with jobs and families: zazen, koan study, talks, ritual and time spent together. He leads a Wednesday evening sitting in eastern Paris, early-morning sittings on Zoom and, since 2026, a semi-residential practice house in Arles where he runs seasonal retreats and a December Rohatsu sesshin. He also co-leads an English-language online study group with Amy Hollowell, offers private interviews and conducts weddings and funerals for anyone who asks. Most of his in-person teaching is in French.

courses.title: Weekly Zen Meditation in Paris, Arles and Online
courses.description: Wednesday evening zazen at the Paris centre near Charonne, Thursday evening and Friday morning sittings in Arles, and two early-morning sittings a week on Zoom. Offered on a donation basis to members of the association.

courses.title: Zen Refuge Study Group (in English)
courses.description: A Saturday-morning group on Zoom, co-led with Amy Hollowell Roshi, that reads koans, sutras and modern Zen writers together as part of practice. It is held in English and needs registration.

free_resources.title: The Dharma and the Ecological Crisis - Sensei Joa Scetbon
free_resources.description: A Zoom dharma talk from 2022 on how Buddhist practice can meet the environmental crisis, published on the Wild Flower Zen Sangha podcast. Free to stream.

English is only part of his teaching: zenrefuge.org is in French, but the Saturday study group is in English and his podcast talk is in English.
The email refugezen@gmail.com is the sangha's shared inbox.

Retreats in Arles (Rohatsu sesshin 10 to 13 Dec 2026; winter 18 to 21 Feb 2027; spring 15 to 18 Apr 2027) share the agenda page, so they are not separate offerings.
